newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI FAILS TO DELIVER AGAINST PIOLINE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUSEDSKI FAILS TO DELIVER AGAINST PIOLINE.

text.p: British tennis was still waiting for its first Wimbledon men's semifinalist for 24 years on Thursday after Greg Rusedski failed to live up to expectations against France's Cedric Pioline.
The Canadian-born Rusedski rarely hinted at the form which propelled him into the last eight as he lost 4-6 6-4 4-6 3-6 in the first instalment of a British 'double bill' on the new Court Number One.
Tim Henman was waiting to face former champion Michael Stich, hoping to emulate Roger Taylor who was the last British man to reach the semifinals.
But Rusedski's challenge petered out tamely on a cool, windy day, his massive serve failing to dig him out of early trouble against Pioline, ranked 44th in the world.
The talented Frenchman, a finalist at the U.S. Open in 1993, broke serve in the opening game of the match and caused his opponent increasing problems with his anticipation and intelligent tactics.

Rusedski did win the second set, spurred on by a fan urging him to 'do it for England', but an astonishing reflex forehand return from Pioline earned an early break in the third and put him on the road to victory.
Pioline becomes only the second Frenchman in the Open era after Henri Leconte in 1986 to reach a Wimbledon semifinal. If he goes on to win the final, he will be the first Gallic winner since 1946.

Henman's surge towards the last four have been assisted by enthusiastic crowds at every match, desperate to assist the 22-year-old's bid to become Britain's first Wimbledon men's singles winner for 61 years.

But there were still plenty of empty seats for much of Rusedski's match which took place amid a generally subdued atmosphere, not helped by a morning start and the divided loyalties of those expected for lunch in the corporate hospitality boxes.
